Constance
KON-stunss
n. (the city on the Rhine at the lake, where the council of 1414 burned Hus, and which was Protestant from 1527 until 1548)
From Latin Constantia, named for the emperor Constantius; German Konstanz.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Constance stands where the Rhine leaves the lake that bears its name, and it was the seat of the largest medieval bishopric north of the Alps. The Council of Constance met there from 1414 to 1418, ended the papal schism by deposing or accepting the resignation of three claimants, condemned the writings of Wyclif, and dealt with Jan Hus, who had come under an imperial safe-conduct from Sigismund, was imprisoned on arrival, refused to abjure articles he said were not his, and was burned on 6 July 1415; Jerome of Prague followed him in 1416. The breaking of the safe-conduct was defended on the ground that no faith need be kept with a heretic. A century later the city itself turned Protestant under Ambrosius Blarer and Johannes Zwick, held out through the 1530s, and was forced back to the old religion by Charles V in 1548 and placed under Austria. The dictionary records Constance for the fire and the safe-conduct. Scripture says the death of God's saints is precious in his sight, and it promises rest and a following record to those who die in the Lord.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines a martyr as one who suffers death for his religion; precious as of great value; to rest as to cease from labour; a witness as one who gives testimony; and faithful as firm in adherence to the truth.

expand to see more

MARTYR, n. One who, by his death, bears witness to the truth of the gospel; one who suffers death in defense of any belief.

PRECIOUS, a. Of great price; costly; of great value or worth; very valuable; highly esteemed.

REST, v.i. To cease from action or motion of any kind; to be quiet or still; to sleep; to lie in death.

WITNESS, n. Testimony; attestation of a fact or event; one who sees or knows a thing and can testify to it.

FAITHFUL, a. Firm in adherence to the truth and to the duties of religion; true to allegiance; constant in affection.

Rev 2:13 — "I know thy works, and where thou dwellest, even where Satan's seat is: and thou holdest fast my name, and hast not denied my faith, even in those days wherein Antipas was my faithful martyr, who was slain among you, where Satan dwelleth."

Heb 11:37 — "They were stoned, they were sawn asunder, were tempted, were slain with the sword: they wandered about in sheepskins and goatskins; being destitute, afflicted, tormented;"

Modern Corruption

Rhine city of the Council of 1414-18, which burned Hus in 1415 under a broken safe-conduct; Protestant from 1527 until forced back by Charles V in 1548.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the value God sets on such a death, which no council can lower: “Precious in the sight of the LORD is the death of his saints” (Psa 116:15). John is told to write it down as a beatitude with a reason attached, “Blessed are the dead which die in the Lord from henceforth” (Rev 14:13).

The live temptation at Constance was the one the council yielded to, which is to decide that promises need not be kept with people who are wrong. A safe-conduct from an emperor was set aside and a man was burned on the strength of that reasoning. Christ's commendation of the church at Pergamos names a single man who died rather than deny, and names him in the middle of a city that killed him: “even in those days wherein Antipas was my faithful martyr, who was slain among you” (Rev 2:13). The catalogue of faith lists the same end without softening it, “They were stoned, they were sawn asunder” (Heb 11:37).

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew yaqar (H3368), precious; Greek makarios (G3107), blessed; Greek martus (G3144), a witness or martyr; Greek anapauo (G0373), to rest.

expand to see more

Hebrew yaqar (H3368) — precious, costly; “Precious in the sight of the LORD is the death of his saints”, Psalm 116:15.

Greek makarios (G3107) — blessed, happy; “Blessed are the dead which die in the Lord”, Revelation 14:13.

Greek anapauo (G0373) — to give rest, to refresh; “that they may rest from their labours”, Revelation 14:13.

Greek martus (G3144) — a witness, a martyr; “Antipas was my faithful martyr”, Revelation 2:13.

Greek prizo (G4249) — to saw asunder; “they were sawn asunder”, Hebrews 11:37.

Usage

"“Precious in the sight of the LORD is the death of his saints” (Psa 116:15) — 6 July 1415."

"“that they may rest from their labours” (Rev 14:13) — written down as a beatitude."

"“who was slain among you” (Rev 2:13) — a city named with its martyr."
